newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB H1 ORDERS RISE 14 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ABB H1 ORDERS RISE 14 PCT.

text.p: Electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said orders received rose 14 percent in the first half of 1997 to $20,049 million.
In local currencies, the rise amounted to 21 percent, ABB said in a statement.

"ABB's 1997 first-half year improvement has been dampened by exchange rate effects, since the ABB Group reports in U.S. dollars and the dollar appreciated against those currencies (mostly European) in which ABB transacts a large protion of its business," the statement said.
ABB also said in its half-year report that the order backlog rose four percent to $35.3 billion.
Expressed in local currencies, the order backlog rose 13 percent.
In orders received, growth was driven mainly by large projects and increased demand from emerging markets as well as by ABB's enhanced focus on sales and marketing.
"Orders for standard products and industrial goods were down somewhat from last year, reflecting the weak demand in many West European markets," ABB said.
"However, expressed in local currencies, orders for these products showed a slight increase," it added.
